plan.title: DESeq2 time-course LRT: treatment-specific trajectory genes
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 2-condition x 4-timepoint (t0-t3), n=3 bulk RNA-seq design (Homo sapiens, 12000 genes x 25 samples incl. 1 extra sample beyond 24, salmon-derived raw counts). The research question — genes with a treatment-specific change over time beyond the shared time trend — is precisely the DESeq2 likelihood-ratio-test (LRT) time-course design: fit the full model ~condition + time + condition:time against the reduced model ~condition + time. Genes surviving this LRT are those whose temporal profile differs by condition, independent of any trend shared by both arms (which the reduced model already absorbs). This is the correct test; a Wald test on a single interaction coefficient would only ask about one time contrast, not the whole trajectory. Track T1 covers QC through DE testing and shrinkage; T2 runs pathway enrichment on the ranked gene list (Hallmark then Reactome/WikiPathways, matched to the human organism); T1S4 clusters the significant genes by their condition-specific trajectory shapes and assembles the final report. All three replicates per cell is the minimum for any replication, so power is limited — this is stated as a caveat at every relevant step, not compensated for by loosening thresholds.

~ condition + time + condition:time, explicit reference levels

trajectory clustering of significant interaction genes + simple effects + power caveats
